blocks.heading: Rewards and motivation
blocks.text: Rewards can influence willingness to work, effort, retention and satisfaction when staff value them and see a credible link between performance and reward. A reward seen as unfair, unattainable or unrelated to a person’s contribution may fail to motivate. Match the arrangement to the task and needs: individual output pay can encourage measurable work, while team recognition can support cooperation. A narrowly defined target can also divert effort from quality or service. Financial incentives do not replace acceptable conditions or solve every problem of monotonous work. Non-financial responsibility needs genuine authority and support, not simply extra duties with blame attached. Review both staff responses and business outcomes rather than assuming a higher payment automatically improves everything.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Eno Packs rewards the number of packs made, while customers complain about poorly sealed packs. The reward can encourage speed but neglects the customer’s quality requirement. Paying for acceptable packs and monitoring quality would align the incentive better, while worker consultation can reveal practical obstacles.
